This invariant guarantees that the log serves as the authoritative source of truth for all committed transactions, even if the data pages themselves are lost or corrupted during a crash.

Transactions are managed through a series of log records that capture the intent and outcome of every operation. Before a transaction modifies any data page, it must first write a "begin" record to the log, followed by "update" records containing the before-image (old value) and after-image (new value) of the modified data.
